title: Finish a rewriter
hints: Look at the two cases inside `simplify`. The `Mul` case calls `simplify` on both children before it rebuilds the node. The `Add` case does not.
After the fix to `Add`, the code still offers the node to `rule` only one time. When `rule` returns a node, that node is new and has not been offered to `rule` yet.
Make the `Add` case `e = Add(simplify(a), simplify(b))`. Then turn the `if` into a loop: `while r is not None:` with `e = r` and `r = rule(e)` inside it.

answer.explain: Both cases now simplify the children first, so by the time `rule` sees a node its sources are already as simple as they get. The `while` loop keeps offering the result to `rule` until it answers `None`, because a rule such as the regrouping one builds a new node, here `(x + 0)`, that another rule can still shrink.
